h1: The 5 Best Food Processors Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Food Processor Under $300: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five food processors that all land well under $300, from a 9-cup Ninja to Hamilton Beach and a two-bowl Ganiza grinder.
summary: The Ninja Professional Plus 9-cup is our best overall, with a 1000-peak-watt motor and Auto-iQ presets. The Hamilton Beach 12-cup is the budget family pick, the Hamilton Beach 10-cup adds a bowl scraper, the Breville is the stainless station, and the Ganiza is the cheapest with two bowls.
intro: A budget ceiling of $300 invites a common mistake: assuming the most expensive machine under the limit is the best one. Every pick here lands well below that ceiling, because above roughly $100 you start paying for brand and finish more than for chopping ability.

We reviewed eight processors and ranked five whose price buckets sit under $200. The two Cuisinart models were dropped because their bucket reaches $500, and the KitchenAid had no price information. Everything here is from listings.

products.name: Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor, 1000PW, 9-Cup, BN601
products.description:
The Ninja BN601 has a 9-cup bowl and a 1000-peak-watt motor, with Auto-iQ preset programs that take the guesswork out of chopping and kneading.

It ranks first because the presets and motor power set it apart from the Hamilton Beach models, though its bowl is smaller than the 12-cup.

Buy it for everyday prep. The caveat is the 9-cup size for large batches.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 12 Cup Stack & Snap Food Processor and Vegetable Chopper
products.verdict: A 12-cup bowl and tool-free assembly in the $50 to $100 bucket.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach has a 12-cup bowl, Stack & Snap tool-free assembly and a vegetable chopper mode.

It ranks second because the capacity beats the Ninja's 9 cups at a lower cost, but it lacks presets.

Best for families. The caveat is fewer features.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Food Processor & Vegetable Chopper, 10 Cups, Stainless Steel
products.verdict: A 10-cup bowl with a built-in scraper and stainless blade.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach pairs its 10-cup bowl with four jobs (slice, shred, mince, puree), a stainless blade, and an included bowl scraper for cleanup.

It ranks third because it sits between the 12-cup and the 9-cup in size and adds a scraper.

Good for cleanup lovers. The caveat is a plain control set.

products.name: Breville All In One Processing Station BSB530XL
products.description:
The Breville BSB530XL is a brushed stainless steel multi-function processing station priced in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks fourth because the listing gives no bowl size or wattage, so it is harder to compare than the Ninja.

Choose it for the design. The caveat is the thin spec detail.
products.skipIf: You compare by capacity and watts.

products.name: Ganiza Food Processor with 2 Bowls, 450W Meat Grinder Vegetable Chopper
products.verdict: The lowest price, with two bowls and meat grinding.
products.description:
The Ganiza has two interchangeable bowls and a 450W motor, with a chopper that can grind meat, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks last because 450W is the lowest power here, but it costs the least.

For light jobs on a tight budget. The caveat is power.
products.idealFor: Light chopping on a small budget.

whatMatters.detail: Bowl capacity in cups sets your batch size. 9 cups handles most weeknights, while 12 suits families. Check the cup figure in the title.
Wattage shows how hard the motor can push through dense food. Peak watts are momentary figures, not steady ones. Check whether the listing says peak.
Presets like Auto-iQ run timed patterns for you. They help new cooks. Look for the preset name in the bullets.
A scraper or tool-free assembly cuts cleanup time. Look for terms such as Easy Clean or Stack & Snap.
A listing that omits bowl size or wattage is harder to judge. Verify those numbers before buying.

faq.q: Why are the Cuisinart models missing?
faq.a: Their price bucket reaches $500, so they may not fit under $300.
Buying by wattage alone. Peak watts are not steady power.

faq.q: Is the Ninja worth it over Hamilton Beach?
faq.a: If you like presets and a stronger motor, yes. Otherwise the 12-cup Hamilton Beach is cheaper.
The Hamilton Beach Stack & Snap assembles without tools.

faq.q: How do I clean the bowl?
faq.a: Use the Easy Clean scraper on the 10-cup Hamilton Beach and rinse promptly.
The Ganiza lists meat grinding, but others do not.

finalTake: The Ninja Professional Plus is the best food processor under $300 here, thanks to presets and power. Choose the Hamilton Beach 12-cup for capacity, the 10-cup for easy cleaning, or the Ganiza for cost. Pick by batch size first.
